written.myAnswer: Science is the organized body of knowledge gained by observing and studying the natural world. Its two main groups are the physical sciences and the biological sciences.

Physics studies matter and energy, their properties and interactions, and their behaviour in space and time. Its branches include mechanics, optics, thermal physics, electromagnetism, nuclear physics, and quantum mechanics.
Interdisciplinary fields combine knowledge and methods from physics and one or more other subjects. Examples include biophysics, astrophysics, geophysics, and computational physics.

Complex problems often involve several kinds of knowledge and cannot be fully solved from one discipline alone. Researchers from different fields collaborate, share and assess evidence, and combine their methods to develop a more complete solution.

Major branches include mechanics, which studies motion and forces; thermal physics, which studies heat and temperature; optics, which studies light; acoustics, which studies sound; electromagnetism, which studies electric and magnetic phenomena; and atomic, nuclear, and particle physics, which study matter at very small scales. Modern branches also include quantum mechanics and relativistic physics.
Interdisciplinary fields of physics combine physics with other subjects. Examples include biophysics, astrophysics, and geophysics.

Science develops knowledge by systematically studying the natural world. Technology applies knowledge to make useful tools or processes. Engineering applies scientific and technological knowledge to design and build solutions. For example, studying the laws of motion is science, a steam-powered device is technology, and designing a machine is engineering.

Physics explains many everyday phenomena involving matter, energy, motion, heat, light, and electricity. It helps explain examples such as objects moving, food heating, light reflecting in a mirror, and electrical appliances operating.
